one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window, both on 2026-10-28: the Q3 2026 earnings webcast and the FOMC decision. 2026-10-31 is a Saturday, so the close that counts is 2026-10-30. Earnings: consensus is about $4.07-4.15 EPS on about $10.8B revenue. Management has guided to a 'very strong' Q3 for orders, and on 2026-10-01 Evercore raised its 2027-28 estimates by 3-4%, said the Q3 setup has improved and pulled the $200B backlog into early 2027. The base rate cuts both ways. GEV's earnings-day reactions have been large and two-sided (+14% in the week after Q1 2026, -9% on Q2 2026 when EPS missed despite +88% orders), and EPS has missed in three of the last eight quarters. A strong order print is now widely expected, so the surprise will come from margins and EPS, where I have no edge. FOMC: Kalshi/Polymarket give hold 74% / hike 26% / cut about 2% (2026-10-01, defirate aggregate). That is 40 points less hike risk than a week ago, but the same markets put about 81% on at least one hike before 2027 (December is 69% hike), so the rate headwind has been delayed, not removed. Short-horizon regularities: the stock bounced about 12% from its mid-September low near $882 (24/7 Wall St, 2026-09-16), including +3.9% today. Short-term reversal and medium-term momentum roughly cancel. I centre the distribution at about $991, essentially flat, with a 15% one-month log sigma. That is slightly above annual vol/3.5 (about 14.9%) to allow for the earnings gap, and the distribution is symmetric in log space.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS about $32.5 x 33x = $1,072), EV/EBITDA (2028E EBITDA $13.1B x 22x + $17B net cash over about 262M shares = $1,165) and FCF yield (about $10.5B 2028E FCF at a 3.5% yield = $1,145), weighted 40/35/25, which gives about $1,120 per share 12 months out.

Industry orders hit a record 38 GW in Q2 2026 (JPMorgan), and new-order pricing is 10-20 points higher. I add only about half of Evercore's premium because GEV EPS has missed in 3 of the last 8 quarters.

Siemens Energy is at about 17x EV/EBITDA and still trades above Barclays' EUR130 peak-cycle target at about EUR144, so the peak-cycle call has not de-rated the group yet. I keep compression from today's level because about 81% hike odds before 2027 (prediction markets) and the GLJ cycle bear case cap the multiple.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2028E FCF about $10.5B at a 3.5% yield = $300B equity value / 262M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener 2028 FCF yield of 4.1% on its roughly $253B market cap.

2026 FCF guidance of $11.5-12.5B is inflated by slot-reservation deposits, and Barclays sees FCF plateauing after 2026 for the sector. 3.5% is a premium-growth industrial yield, near the 3.2-4.1% consensus range for 2027-28.

bear.story: The cycle turns. Orders fade from a roughly 150 GW annualised Q2 2026 pace toward Barclays' sustainable 80-90 GW. Slot reservations stop converting. The AI capex digestion that Polymarket prices at about 18% by mid-2027 (thin market) arrives, or the Fed hikes into a slowdown. The multiple falls to about 20x a roughly $32 EPS, close to Siemens Energy's level. Base-rate precedent: global gas awards fell from about 100 GW in 2000 to about 30 GW by 2003, and GEV fell 15% in a week on DeepSeek in January 2025. GLJ's $470 target is the tail of this case.

base.story: Execution continues: backlog reaches $200B in early 2027, Electrification margins hold at 18-20%, Wind losses narrow, and 2028 EPS of about $34-35 holds with modest upward revisions. The multiple drifts to about 33x NTM, so the price rises roughly in line with EPS less multiple compression.

bull.story: Orders and pricing keep beating: industry orders hold above 120 GW a year, turbine prices head to WoodMac's $600/kW, 2028 targets are raised at the December 2026 investor update and 2032 slots fill. EPS momentum holds a 38-40x multiple and the stock clears the $1,196 high, close to Guggenheim's $1,450 target.

thesis_break_reason: At about $650 GEV would trade near 19-20x 2028E consensus EPS, about Siemens Energy's level, so the market would no longer pay any growth premium. That is -34% from here, well beyond the roughly 26% drawdowns of 2026 (from $1,196 to about $882 in mid-September). A move that large would most likely mean something fundamental broke: slot reservations failing to convert or orders being cancelled, a hyperscaler capex cut, a large margin miss in Power or Electrification, or the market concluding the cycle has peaked as it did in 2001-02.

reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with the search budget restored (about 22 more searches and fetches). Anchor: realised vol is 52%. In 2026 alone the stock had a roughly 26% drawdown (June high $1,196 to about $882 in mid-September) and earnings-week moves of +14% and -9%, so I use a three-component lognormal mixture with an effective sigma of about 40%. New evidence on the bull side: global gas-turbine orders hit a record 38 GW in Q2 2026 (JPMorgan, +71% y/y), which pushes against Barclays' July peak call. Siemens Energy still trades above Barclays' target. New GEV pricing is 10-20 points above Q4 2025. The CEO says 2032 slots are selling. Evercore raised 2027-28 estimates on 2026-10-01 and pulled the $200B backlog into early 2027. Vineyard Wind settled on 2026-09-16. New evidence on the bear side: GLJ initiated at Sell with a $470 target on 2026-09-14, arguing 2029-31 overcapacity (104-113 GW against 88-90 GW of demand). Prediction markets price about 81% odds of a Fed hike before 2027. Polymarket puts an AI-bubble burst at 18% by mid-2027. The 2000-03 base rate (awards fell from about 100 GW to about 30 GW) shows how hard this cycle can turn. Academic work finds target-implied returns exceed realised returns by about 15-35%. I therefore treat the $1,237-1,250 Street mean/median as an upper anchor, which puts it near my base case plus some upside. Net: fair value rises from $1,100 to $1,120 (P/E method $1,021 to $1,072); EV/EBITDA and FCF yield are unchanged. Scenarios: 25% bear at $650, 50% base at $1,090 (was $1,070), 25% bull at $1,450 (was $1,430). Mixture mean is about $1,070 (+8%), median about $1,075, P(at or above today's price) 0.60 (was 0.58). No options data consulted, and nothing under priors/ was opened.
